scope: Where the Rust rewrite's structure still differs from the Go owner it ports, from the 2026-11-22 file-level re-audit (method in structural-audit-2026-11-22.md).

findings.finding: ANALYZE is not in Go's shape. One 3,055-line `real_tikv_analyze.rs` holds the planner's `buildAnalyze*` / `getMustAnalyzedColumns`, the executor's `AnalyzeExec` and globalstats' async merge; Go's `AnalyzeExec` worker pool (`analyzeWorker`, `handleResultsError`, `handleGlobalStats`), `AnalyzeColumnsExec`'s sampling build (`buildSamplingStats`, `subMergeWorker`, `subBuildWorker`, `readDataAndSendTask`, `handleNDVForSpecialIndexes`), `analyze_idx.go`'s `fetchAnalyzeResult`, `analyze_global_stats.go` and `analyze_worker.go` have no counterparts.

Go's `findBestTask` compares data-source cop tasks through `getTaskPlanCost` (an index-lookup cop task's table side priced without `isChildOfINL`, the result cached on each operator by `PlanCostInit`, which the IndexLookUp reader then reuses); this planner converts candidates to root tasks before `compare_task_cost`, so no cop task is ever compared. Plans matched on every probe, but the pricing calls differ: EXPLAIN EXPLORE's recorded variables miss `tidb_opt_table_range_scan_cost_factor` for an index-lookup TopN query, and per-operator cost caching is not reproduced.
findings.rust_evidence: `tidb-planner/src/find_best_task/dispatch.rs` (only root tasks reach `compare_task_cost` for the TestRelevantOptVarsAndFixes queries), `find_best_task/coster.rs` (no per-operator cost cache)
